lesson.child_mission: Number patterns follow a rule. Find the rule by looking at how terms change, then use it to continue or find a missing term.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same method to a larger number or a new context, then compare two solution paths for accuracy.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Find the rule and the missing term: 1,200; 1,500; ___; 2,100.

FEEDBACK
Rule: add 300. Missing term 1,800.

WATCH FOR
Looking only at the first digit and ignoring the add/subtract rule leads to false terms.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
For four sequences (two increasing, two decreasing), state the rule, fill one missing term and write the next two terms. Use different intervals such as 5, 10, 50 and 100.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Number patterns follow a rule. Find the rule by looking at how terms change, then use it to continue or find a missing term.
materials: Optional: place-value chart or number line
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: For four sequences (two increasing, two decreasing), state the rule, fill one missing term and write the next two terms. Use different intervals such as 5, 10, 50 and 100. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new numbers solved with visible working for pattern; key places/values named. Do not award marks for retyping the model.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Looking only at the first digit and ignoring the add/subtract rule leads to false terms.. Correction uses Rule: add 300. Missing term 1,800.. Why: restores accurate pattern.

Parent: Likely misconception: Looking only at the first digit and ignoring the add/subtract rule leads to false terms. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses pattern with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with pattern, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept any mathematically valid solution that uses new numbers, shows working for pattern, and names places/values. Reject copied model numbers. / Accept a named misconception about pattern, corrected working, and a method reason. Reject vague “I was wrong” with no repair..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Sequence 405, 415, 425, 435 increases by 10 each time. The next term is 445.

TRY FIRST
Find the rule and the missing term: 1,200; 1,500; ___; 2,100.

FEEDBACK
Rule: add 300. Missing term 1,800.
teach_steps.explain:
Number patterns follow a rule. Find the rule by looking at how terms change, then use it to continue or find a missing term.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Looking only at the first digit and ignoring the add/subtract rule leads to false terms. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
teach_steps.title: Understand and model
